newsitem.title: USA: U.S. says Mars probe back in Earth's atmosphere.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says Mars probe back in Earth's atmosphere.

text.p: The United States Space Command said it estimates that Russia's disabled Mars probe re-entered the Earth's atmosphere at 8:19 P.M. EST over the southern Pacific Ocean.

The information was based on sensors and it was not immediately clear where exactly the spacecraft landed. Final confirmation that it was back on Earth would be possible only after the completion of its next scheduled orbit past the sensors, just after 9 P.M. EST, a spokeswoman for U.S. Space Command said. "It it doesn't show up, we'll know it definitely re-entered," she said.
A U.S. official said earlier that the probe was estimated to splash down some 500 miles (800 km) southeast of New Zealand.
U.S. National Security Council official Robert Bell told CNN that the impact zone was calculated on the last orbit the spacecraft made before re-entering the Earth's atmosphere.
He said the satellite was travelling at 17,000 miles per hour and would take only a few minutes to re-enter the atmopshere and hit the ocean.
The six-tonne Mars probe, carrying 200 grammes of plutonium in four battery-canisters, blasted off from Kazakhstan on Saturday but failed to make it into orbit around earth.
